User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the SETU application, storing their selected role and basic profile information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

role.description: The role selected by the user, determining their application experience. (Enum: Child, Parent, Teacher)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Conversation.title: Conversation
Conversation.description: Represents a single mediated interaction, including the original message, its AI-processed reframed version, and associated metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Conversation entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who initiated this conversation. (Relationship: User 1:N Conversation)

originalMessageText.description: The transcribed text of the user's original voice input.

originalAudioS3Url.description: URL to the original audio recording of the user's message, stored in AWS S3.

originalLanguageCode.description: The language code of the original message (e.g., 'en', 'mr').

originalSentiment.description: The detected sentiment of the original message (e.g., 'POSITIVE', 'NEUTRAL', 'NEGATIVE', 'MIXED').

originalSentimentConfidence.description: Confidence score of the detected sentiment for the original message.

reframedMessageText.description: The AI-reframed and mediated version of the message.

reframedAudioS3Url.description: URL to the audio file of the reframed message, generated by AWS Polly and stored in AWS S3.

reframedLanguageCode.description: The language code of the reframed message (e.g., 'en', 'mr').

reframedSentiment.description: The detected sentiment of the reframed message (e.g., 'POSITIVE', 'NEUTRAL', 'NEGATIVE', 'MIXED').

mediationExplanation.description: An explanation provided by the AI regarding how the message was reframed.

safetyCheckStatus.description: Status indicating the result of the safety check on the message (e.g., 'SAFE', 'FLAGGED', 'UNKNOWN').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this conversation record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this conversation record was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. Access is restricted to the owner of the profile via 'request.auth.uid'. The 'role' field is stored here for DBAC-based authorization. No denormalization needed as this is a root entity for the user.

Stores individual conversations belonging to a specific user. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence, allowing security rules to verify ownership without 'get()' calls on the parent user document. Access is restricted to the authenticated 'userId' matching the path parameter.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this conversation.

params.name: conversationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the conversation.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security Rules (QAPs), leveraging structural segregation and hierarchical paths for robust security. 

**User Profile Management:**
User profiles are stored in a top-level collection `/users/{userId}`. This path directly maps the document ID to the authenticated user's UID (`request.auth.uid`), ensuring that each user can only read and write their own profile. The `User` entity includes a `role` field (Child, Parent, Teacher) which is stored directly in the user's document. This adheres to the DBAC principle, allowing security rules to authorize based on database-stored roles without relying on custom claims or `get()` operations on other collections.

**Conversation Management (Authorization Independence & QAPs):**
User-owned conversations are stored in a subcollection under the respective user's profile: `/users/{userId}/conversations/{conversationId}`. This hierarchical structure provides inherent ownership, making security rules straightforward: only the `userId` matching the path wildcard can access their own conversations. 

**Crucially, this structure achieves Authorization Independence by having the `Conversation` document explicitly include the `userId` field within its own data (`resource.data.userId`).** This is a direct application of the 'Authorization Independence via Denormalization' mandate. Because the `userId` is present in every `Conversation` document, Firestore security rules can verify ownership by comparing `request.auth.uid` with `resource.data.userId` AND `userId` (from the path parameter) without needing to perform a `get()` operation on the parent `/users/{userId}` document. This eliminates complex `get()` calls in rules, making them atomic, more efficient, and easier to debug, as it avoids dependencies on parent document attributes during batch writes or transactions.

**Support for QAPs (Query-Aware Security Rules):**
The structural segregation and hierarchical path for conversations directly support QAPs. A user can only `list` conversations from their *own* `/users/{request.auth.uid}/conversations` subcollection. Any attempt to `list` conversations from another user's subcollection (e.g., `/users/someOtherId/conversations`) will be automatically denied by rules that enforce `request.auth.uid == userId`. This means that `list` operations are implicitly secure; the structure itself ensures that queries cannot accidentally or maliciously expose unauthorized data, as rules are applied at the document level and path segments. There is no need for rules to act as filters after data has been fetched, ensuring that only authorized data is ever returned by a query.
